title: Claude Code plugin marketplace (marketplace.json, versions, release tags, team settings)

rules.rule: Change plugin.json `version` in every release meant to reach users, and only there.
rules.why: Installed copies are cached by computed version: if new commits are pushed without changing `version`, users stay on their cached copy and never receive them (auto-update and `claude plugin update` both compare versions).

rules.rule: Do not set `version` on the marketplace entry; keep it in plugin.json alone.
rules.why: When both are set, plugin.json wins silently at install, and `claude plugin validate` warns `Entry declares version ... but plugin.json says ...`, which fails CI under `--strict`. A second copy also drifts from the tag.
rules.repoConvention: The test tolerates an entry version equal to plugin.json; the docs say not to set it in both places at all.

rules.rule: Create release tags with `claude plugin tag plugins/stackfoundry` (dry-run first), never by hand, and never force-move or reuse a `stackfoundry--v<version>` tag.
rules.why: Dependency ranges resolve against `<plugin>--v<version>` tags and constraint checks use the tag's version, not plugin.json. `claude plugin tag` validates the plugin, checks plugin.json and the marketplace entry agree, requires a clean tree and refuses an existing tag; a hand-made or force-moved tag can name a version whose content differs, and the next install fetches the moved commit.

rules.rule: Never change the marketplace `name` or the plugin `name`; change the visible label with `displayName`. If a plugin name must change or an entry is removed, add an append-only top-level `renames` map (old -> new or null).
rules.why: `stackfoundry@stackfoundry` is the install id and the key in users' `enabledPlugins`, `pluginConfigs` and `extraKnownMarketplaces`; a rename breaks every existing install with `Plugin "<name>" not found in marketplace`. Editing an old `renames` entry instead of appending breaks the chain Claude Code follows from the oldest name.

rules.rule: Keep the marketplace entry `name` identical to plugin.json `name`.
rules.why: The entry name is the install id; the manifest name is the skill prefix. When they differ, installing by the manifest name fails with `Plugin "<manifest-name>" not found in marketplace`.

rules.rule: Write a relative `source` from the marketplace root with a leading `./`, forward slashes and no `..`, and distribute the marketplace as a git repository (`owner/repo`), never as a bare marketplace.json URL.
rules.why: A path with `..` or without `./` fails validation; a path to a missing directory passes validation and fails only at install (`Source path does not exist`). A URL-added marketplace downloads only marketplace.json, so every relative-path entry fails at install.

rules.rule: Validate with `--strict` on both the marketplace root and the plugin directory, at a pinned CLI version.
rules.why: Claude Code ignores unknown keys at load time, so a typo in a field loads silently; only `--strict` turns the `Unknown field` warning into a failure. A marketplace-root run does not open the skill, agent, command or hook files of the listed plugin, so the plugin needs its own run.

rules.rule: Key the project-scope `extraKnownMarketplaces` entry by the marketplace `name` (`stackfoundry`) with a `github` source, and pair it with `enabledPlugins["stackfoundry@stackfoundry"]`; skip both in the marketplace repo itself.
rules.why: Repository `extraKnownMarketplaces` applies only after the contributor accepts the folder trust dialog and is ignored without a message in an untrusted folder (and in `-p` runs unless trust was accepted before); a key that differs from the marketplace name registers nothing usable.
where: plugins/stackfoundry/skills/init/SKILL.md section 4, settings.json row and 'A repo that is itself the stackfoundry marketplace'

rules.rule: Do not add `strict`, component fields, `headers`/`headersHelper` or `dependencies` to the marketplace entry; declare components in the plugin directory.
rules.why: With `strict: false` an entry that declares components makes the plugin fail to load (`conflicting manifests`); entry `hooks` written as a path pass validation and never run; `headers` on a non-archive source have no effect.

bugCategories.name: unreleased-change
bugCategories.lookFor: A diff that changes files under plugins/stackfoundry/ for users without changing plugin.json `version` (and the CHANGELOG section) before tagging.
bugCategories.failure: Users on the cached version never receive the change; auto-update sees nothing new.

bugCategories.name: identifier-rename
bugCategories.lookFor: Any edit to marketplace.json `name`, a plugins[].name, or plugin.json `name`, or removal of an entry, without a matching `renames` entry.
bugCategories.failure: Every existing install and every repo's enabledPlugins/extraKnownMarketplaces key stops resolving (`not found in marketplace`).

bugCategories.name: version-drift
bugCategories.lookFor: A version on the marketplace entry, a tag created with plain `git tag`, or a tag whose version differs from plugin.json at the tagged commit.
bugCategories.failure: plugin.json silently wins over the entry; dependents resolve a tag whose content does not match its version.

bugCategories.name: unresolvable-source
bugCategories.lookFor: A relative `source` without `./`, with `..`, with backslashes, or pointing at a directory that does not exist; instructions that add the marketplace by a raw marketplace.json URL.
bugCategories.failure: Validation may pass (missing directory) while every install fails with `Source path does not exist` or a path-outside-marketplace error.

bugCategories.name: silently-ignored-field
bugCategories.lookFor: A misspelled or unsupported key in marketplace.json or the entry (e.g. a field meant for plugin.json, entry `hooks` as a path).
bugCategories.failure: Claude Code ignores it at load, so the intended behaviour never happens; only `validate --strict` or a load error reveals it.

testing.layers: Unit tests prove the two manifests agree (names, source path, semver, no conflicting version); `claude plugin validate --strict` proves the schema; `claude plugin tag --dry-run` proves tag/version agreement before a release; only an install from the pushed marketplace proves the source resolves.
traps: A relative source pointing at a missing directory passes validate; assert the path exists and stays inside the root (the test resolves it but does not check `./` prefix or absence of `..`).
Validating the marketplace root does not open the plugin's component files; keep the separate plugin run.
Local edits from a marketplace added by local path load in place without a version bump, so a local test cannot show that users would miss an unbumped release.

security.note: A plugin runs hooks and its bin/ executables with the user's full privileges, outside the sandbox, and auto-update replaces reviewed files without re-approval. Treat any release diff touching hooks/hooks.json, bin/ or scripts/ as security-relevant for every installed user.

Marketplace names that imitate official Anthropic names, contain non-ASCII characters, or match reserved names are refused, and an already-registered one stops loading with its plugins. `stackfoundry` is not reserved; keep any future marketplace name ASCII and distinct.

lockStep: plugin.json version <-> plugins/stackfoundry/CHANGELOG.md section <-> tag stackfoundry--v<version>
marketplace.json name <-> extraKnownMarketplaces key and enabledPlugins id in init/SKILL.md and both READMEs
